meta.method: Every entry with status 'verified' was built from zoning chapter text loaded directly from the jurisdiction's own codifier or document center on the verifiedOn date. Entries with status 'unverified' name a zone the live MLS feed uses but whose chapter could not be loaded. Unverified entries state no minimums and answer every intent question with 'check'.

intentSemantics.adu: What the zoning code says about accessory dwelling units at the zone level. Never a statement about a specific property.
intentSemantics.str: What the jurisdiction's code says about short term rentals at the zone level. Eligibility for a specific property is never asserted. See stateLaw and each entry's notes.

urbanAdu.summary: Cities over 2,500 people must allow at least one accessory dwelling unit on each lot zoned for detached single family homes inside the urban growth boundary, subject to reasonable siting and design rules. Owner occupancy and extra parking cannot be required.

middleHousing.summary: Cities of 25,000 or more must allow duplexes, triplexes, quadplexes, cottage clusters and townhouses on lots that allow detached single family homes. Cities from 2,500 to 24,999 must allow a duplex.

ruralAdu.summary: Counties have the option to allow one accessory dwelling unit on rural residential land with a 2 acre minimum, an existing single family dwelling, and wildfire conditions. It is not a mandate and it does not reach farm zones. Deschutes County implements it at DCC 18.116.355.

efu.summary: Defines exclusive farm use and the farm-use test that governs what happens on EFU zoned land.

deschutes-county:RR10.name: Rural Residential Zone (RR-10)
deschutes-county:RR10.plainEnglish: County zone for rural homesites. One home per lot is allowed outright, along with farm use and noncommercial horse stables. New lots need at least 10 acres.
deschutes-county:RR10.notes: DCC 18.116.355 allows one accessory dwelling unit outright on an RR-10 or MUA-10 lot when the lot is at least 2 acres (5 acres in some unsewered townships south of Sunriver), an existing single family home is on the lot, and the unit stays within 900 sq ft of usable floor area. Fire protection and wastewater conditions apply.

deschutes-county:MUA10.name: Multiple Use Agricultural Zone (MUA)
deschutes-county:MUA10.plainEnglish: County zone for part-time farms and rural living on land not suited to full-time commercial farming. One home per lot, agriculture, and noncommercial horse stables are allowed outright. New lots need at least 10 acres.
deschutes-county:MUA10.notes: DCC 18.116.355 allows one accessory dwelling unit outright on an RR-10 or MUA-10 lot when the lot is at least 2 acres (5 acres in some unsewered townships south of Sunriver), an existing single family home is on the lot, and the unit stays within 900 sq ft of usable floor area. Fire protection and wastewater conditions apply.

deschutes-county:EFU.name: Exclusive Farm Use Zones
deschutes-county:EFU.plainEnglish: Farmland preservation zone. Farm use is the primary use and dwellings follow state farm-use tests. Minimum sizes for new parcels vary by subzone under DCC 18.16.065. Check with Deschutes County planning before assuming a home site.
deschutes-county:EFU.notes: The county's rural ADU standard (DCC 18.116.355) applies to RR-10 and MUA-10 lots, not EFU land. Farm dwellings follow separate state tests. Check with Deschutes County planning.

deschutes-county:EFUTRB.name: Exclusive Farm Use Zone, Tumalo/Redmond/Bend Subzone
deschutes-county:EFUTRB.plainEnglish: Farmland preservation zone in the Tumalo/Redmond/Bend subzone. Farm use is the primary use and dwellings follow state farm-use tests. Check with Deschutes County planning before assuming a home site.
deschutes-county:EFUTRB.minLotSize: 23 irrigated acres to create a new irrigated parcel (DCC 18.16.065)

deschutes-county:EFUSC.name: Exclusive Farm Use Zone, Sisters/Cloverdale Subzone
deschutes-county:EFUSC.plainEnglish: Farmland preservation zone in the Sisters/Cloverdale subzone. Farm use is the primary use and dwellings follow state farm-use tests. Check with Deschutes County planning before assuming a home site.
deschutes-county:EFUSC.minLotSize: 63 irrigated acres to create a new irrigated parcel (DCC 18.16.065)

deschutes-county:EFUAL.name: Exclusive Farm Use Zone, Alfalfa Subzone
deschutes-county:EFUAL.plainEnglish: Farmland preservation zone in the Alfalfa subzone. Farm use is the primary use and dwellings follow state farm-use tests. Check with Deschutes County planning before assuming a home site.
deschutes-county:EFUAL.minLotSize: 36 irrigated acres to create a new irrigated parcel (DCC 18.16.065)

deschutes-county:EFUTE.name: Exclusive Farm Use Zone, Terrebonne Subzone
deschutes-county:EFUTE.plainEnglish: Farmland preservation zone in the Terrebonne subzone. Farm use is the primary use and dwellings follow state farm-use tests. Check with Deschutes County planning before assuming a home site.
deschutes-county:EFUTE.minLotSize: 35 irrigated acres to create a new irrigated parcel (DCC 18.16.065)

deschutes-county:EFULB.name: Exclusive Farm Use Zone, Lower Bridge Subzone
deschutes-county:EFULB.plainEnglish: Farmland preservation zone in the Lower Bridge subzone. Farm use is the primary use and dwellings follow state farm-use tests. Check with Deschutes County planning before assuming a home site.
deschutes-county:EFULB.minLotSize: 130 irrigated acres to create a new irrigated parcel (DCC 18.16.065)

deschutes-county:EFULA.name: Exclusive Farm Use Zone, La Pine Subzone
deschutes-county:EFULA.plainEnglish: Farmland preservation zone in the La Pine subzone. Farm use is the primary use and dwellings follow state farm-use tests. Check with Deschutes County planning before assuming a home site.
deschutes-county:EFULA.minLotSize: 37 irrigated acres to create a new irrigated parcel (DCC 18.16.065)

deschutes-county:EFUHR.name: Exclusive Farm Use Zone, Horse Ridge East Subzone
deschutes-county:EFUHR.plainEnglish: Farmland preservation zone in the Horse Ridge East subzone. Farm use is the primary use and dwellings follow state farm-use tests. Check with Deschutes County planning before assuming a home site.

deschutes-county:UAR10.name: Urban Area Reserve Zone (UAR-10)
deschutes-county:UAR10.plainEnglish: County holding zone at the edge of Bend's urban growth boundary, kept in large lots until urban growth reaches it. One home per lot and farm uses are allowed. New lots need at least 10 acres.
deschutes-county:UAR10.notes: A residential accessory dwelling unit is a permitted use subject to the standards in DCC 19.92.160.

deschutes-county:F1.name: Forest Use Zone (F-1)
deschutes-county:F1.plainEnglish: County forest zone named in the DCC Title 18 chapter index. The chapter text was not loaded for this build, so no standards are stated here. Check with Deschutes County planning.
deschutes-county:F1.sourceCite: DCC 18.36 (chapter title from the Title 18 index)

deschutes-county:F2.name: Forest Use Zone (F-2)
deschutes-county:F2.plainEnglish: County forest zone named in the DCC Title 18 chapter index. The chapter text was not loaded for this build, so no standards are stated here. Check with Deschutes County planning.
deschutes-county:F2.sourceCite: DCC 18.40 (chapter title from the Title 18 index)

bend:RS.name: Standard Density Residential District (RS)
bend:RS.plainEnglish: Bend's most common residential zone, with a wide variety of housing types at 4.0 to 7.3 dwelling units per gross acre where sewer and water are available.
bend:RS.notes: ORS 197A.425 requires cities over 2,500 people to allow at least one accessory dwelling unit on lots zoned for detached single family homes inside the urban growth boundary. Local siting and design standards apply. Bend's standards live in BDC 3.6.200. BDC 3.6.500 requires a short term rental permit and enforces a 500 foot separation between permitted short term rentals in the RL, RS, RM and RH districts.

bend:RL.name: Low Density Residential District (RL)
bend:RL.plainEnglish: Large urban residential lots at 1.1 to 4.0 dwelling units per gross acre, served by community water and sewer or septic systems.
bend:RL.notes: ORS 197A.425 requires cities over 2,500 people to allow at least one accessory dwelling unit on lots zoned for detached single family homes inside the urban growth boundary. Local siting and design standards apply. Bend's standards live in BDC 3.6.200. BDC 3.6.500 requires a short term rental permit and enforces a 500 foot separation between permitted short term rentals in the RL, RS, RM and RH districts.

bend:RM.name: Medium Density Residential District (RM)
bend:RM.plainEnglish: Primarily multi-unit residential at 7.3 to 21.7 units per gross acre, acting as a transition between other residential districts and busier areas.
bend:RM.notes: BDC 3.6.500 requires a short term rental permit and enforces a 500 foot separation between permitted short term rentals in the RL, RS, RM and RH districts.

bend:RM-10.name: Medium-10 Density Residential District (RM-10)
bend:RM-10.plainEnglish: Residential district for manufactured dwelling parks and a variety of single and multi-unit housing at 6.0 to 10.0 dwelling units per gross acre.
bend:RM-10.notes: BDC 3.6.500 requires a short term rental permit and enforces a 500 foot separation between permitted short term rentals in the RL, RS, RM and RH districts.

bend:RH.name: High Density Residential District (RH)
bend:RH.plainEnglish: High density multi-unit residential near shopping, services and transit, with a minimum density of 21.7 units per gross acre and no maximum.
bend:RH.notes: BDC 3.6.500 requires a short term rental permit and enforces a 500 foot separation between permitted short term rentals in the RL, RS, RM and RH districts.

bend:UAR.name: Urban Area Reserve District (UAR)
bend:UAR.plainEnglish: Holding zone for future urban development inside Bend, capped at 1 dwelling unit per 10 gross acres until land is rezoned.

redmond:R-1.name: R-1 Limited Residential Zone
redmond:R-1.plainEnglish: Lower density residential neighborhoods for single family detached homes, middle housing, and a mix of other housing types.
redmond:R-1.notes: ORS 197A.425 requires cities over 2,500 people to allow at least one accessory dwelling unit on lots zoned for detached single family homes inside the urban growth boundary. Local siting and design standards apply. Check with the City of Redmond for its standards.
redmond:R-1.sourceCite: Redmond Development Code, Chapter 8 Article I, Establishment of Zones and Districts

redmond:R-2.name: R-2 Limited Residential Zone
redmond:R-2.plainEnglish: Low density residential neighborhoods for single family detached homes, middle housing, and a mix of other housing types.
redmond:R-2.notes: ORS 197A.425 requires cities over 2,500 people to allow at least one accessory dwelling unit on lots zoned for detached single family homes inside the urban growth boundary. Local siting and design standards apply. Check with the City of Redmond for its standards.
redmond:R-2.sourceCite: Redmond Development Code, Chapter 8 Article I, Establishment of Zones and Districts

redmond:R-3.name: R-3 Limited Residential Zone
redmond:R-3.plainEnglish: Medium density residential neighborhoods with a mix of single family detached homes, middle housing, and other housing types.
redmond:R-3.notes: ORS 197A.425 requires cities over 2,500 people to allow at least one accessory dwelling unit on lots zoned for detached single family homes inside the urban growth boundary. Local siting and design standards apply. Check with the City of Redmond for its standards.
redmond:R-3.sourceCite: Redmond Development Code, Chapter 8 Article I, Establishment of Zones and Districts

redmond:R-4.name: R-4 General Residential Zone
redmond:R-4.plainEnglish: Medium density residential neighborhoods with single family homes, middle housing, and multi-family development. Offices are conditionally permitted where compatible.
redmond:R-4.notes: ORS 197A.425 requires cities over 2,500 people to allow at least one accessory dwelling unit on lots zoned for detached single family homes inside the urban growth boundary. Local siting and design standards apply. Check with the City of Redmond for its standards.
redmond:R-4.sourceCite: Redmond Development Code, Chapter 8 Article I, Establishment of Zones and Districts

redmond:R-5.name: R-5 High Density Residential Zone
redmond:R-5.plainEnglish: High density residential neighborhoods with an emphasis on multi-family development, middle housing, and smaller lot single family homes.
redmond:R-5.notes: ORS 197A.425 requires cities over 2,500 people to allow at least one accessory dwelling unit on lots zoned for detached single family homes inside the urban growth boundary. Local siting and design standards apply. Check with the City of Redmond for its standards.
redmond:R-5.sourceCite: Redmond Development Code, Chapter 8 Article I, Establishment of Zones and Districts

redmond:UH-10.name: UH-10 Urban Holding Zone
redmond:UH-10.plainEnglish: Holding zone that keeps large undeveloped areas agricultural until urbanization. Annexation, master plan approval, or a zone change is required before urban development.
redmond:UH-10.sourceCite: Redmond Development Code, Chapter 8 Article I, Establishment of Zones and Districts

redmond:MUN.name: MUN Mixed-Use Neighborhood Zone
redmond:MUN.plainEnglish: Neighborhood scale mix of retail, service, civic and residential uses. Residential is combined with commercial as mixed use or live-work. The district itself has a 3 acre minimum size.
redmond:MUN.sourceCite: Redmond Development Code, Chapter 8 Article I, MUN Mixed-Use Neighborhood Zone

sisters:R.name: Residential District (R)
sisters:R.plainEnglish: Sisters' main residential zone with single family homes, duplexes, manufactured homes and cottage development. A single family detached lot needs at least 4,500 sq ft.
sisters:R.minLotSize: 4,500 sq ft for a single family detached lot (SDC Table 2.2.2)
sisters:R.notes: SDC 2.15.300 allows one accessory dwelling unit per lot up to 800 sq ft of living area through a Type I review. SDC 2.15.2700 requires a short term rental permit, bars a new short term rental within 500 feet of another approved one in the residential districts, and voids the approval when the property transfers. The buyer must reapply.

sisters:MFR.name: Multi-Family Residential District (MFR)
sisters:MFR.plainEnglish: Residential district for a range of housing types and lot sizes with minimum and maximum density standards, designed to neighborhood scale.
sisters:MFR.notes: SDC 2.15.300 allows one accessory dwelling unit per lot up to 800 sq ft of living area through a Type I review. SDC 2.15.2700 requires a short term rental permit, bars a new short term rental within 500 feet of another approved one in the residential districts, and voids the approval when the property transfers. The buyer must reapply.

la-pine:RSF.name: Residential Single Family (RSF)
la-pine:RSF.plainEnglish: City residential zone. The La Pine Development Code files were unreachable on the city site at verification time, so no standards are stated here. Check with the City of La Pine.
la-pine:RSF.sourceCite: La Pine Development Code (city site restructure broke the code links on 2026-07-30)

madras:R-1.name: Moderate Density Residential (R-1)
madras:R-1.plainEnglish: Madras' larger lot residential zone with a broad range of housing types and essential development standards.
madras:R-1.notes: MDC Table 18.15.040-2 permits one accessory dwelling unit in conjunction with one single detached dwelling.

madras:R-2.name: Higher Density Residential (R-2)
madras:R-2.plainEnglish: Residential neighborhoods with a mix of uses that buffer commercial areas, including multi-unit dwellings and middle housing near existing commercial uses.
madras:R-2.notes: MDC Table 18.15.040-2 permits one accessory dwelling unit in conjunction with one single detached dwelling.

madras:R-3.name: Planned Residential Development (R-3)
madras:R-3.plainEnglish: Residential zone for areas of scenic quality, with flexible project design that works with the natural topography of the site.
madras:R-3.notes: MDC Table 18.15.040-2 permits one accessory dwelling unit in conjunction with one single detached dwelling.

madras:MUE.name: Mixed-Use Employment (MUE)
madras:MUE.plainEnglish: Employment zone for business parks, offices, light manufacturing, warehousing and retail. Single family housing is not permitted as a standalone use.

prineville:R-1.name: Limited Residential R-1 Zone
prineville:R-1.plainEnglish: Preserves Prineville's predominantly single family, owner occupied neighborhoods such as Ochoco Heights and Northridge.
prineville:R-1.notes: ORS 197A.425 requires cities over 2,500 people to allow at least one accessory dwelling unit on lots zoned for detached single family homes inside the urban growth boundary. Local siting and design standards apply. Prineville's standards live in city code 153.080. Check with the City of Prineville.

prineville:R-2.name: General Residential R-2 Zone
prineville:R-2.plainEnglish: Residential areas that mix a variety of housing types at various densities, with limited convenience commercial services for nearby residents.
prineville:R-2.notes: ORS 197A.425 requires cities over 2,500 people to allow at least one accessory dwelling unit on lots zoned for detached single family homes inside the urban growth boundary. Local siting and design standards apply. Prineville's standards live in city code 153.080. Check with the City of Prineville.

prineville:PR.name: Open Space-Park Reserve PR Zone
prineville:PR.plainEnglish: Protects natural resources, recreation land and open space in and around Prineville, and limits development in environmentally sensitive areas.

jefferson-county:A-1.name: Exclusive Farm Use A-1 (EFU A-1)
jefferson-county:A-1.plainEnglish: Preserves predominantly irrigated agricultural soils for farm use. Dwellings follow state farm-use tests. Check with Jefferson County Community Development before assuming a home site.

jefferson-county:A-2.name: Exclusive Farm Use A-2 (EFU A-2)
jefferson-county:A-2.plainEnglish: Preserves agricultural land that is less productive than A-1 land due to soil class and lack of irrigation. Dwellings follow state farm-use tests. Check with Jefferson County Community Development before assuming a home site.

jefferson-county:RL.name: Range Land (RL)
jefferson-county:RL.plainEnglish: Preserves predominantly non-irrigated agricultural soils used for livestock grazing. Dwellings follow state farm-use tests. Check with Jefferson County Community Development before assuming a home site.

jefferson-county:RR-2.name: Rural Residential (RR-2)
jefferson-county:RR-2.plainEnglish: Low density rural homesites in an open space setting. One single family home per parcel is allowed outright, along with crops and livestock. New parcels need at least 2 acres.
jefferson-county:RR-2.notes: Jefferson County's codified RR zone text (JCC 17.304) permits an accessory dwelling unit only in the urban growth area, while the county separately publishes a countywide rural ADU policy at jeffersoncountyor.gov. The two sources disagree, so this ships as a question for the county. Check with Jefferson County Community Development.

jefferson-county:RR-5.name: Rural Residential (RR-5)
jefferson-county:RR-5.plainEnglish: Low density rural homesites in an open space setting. One single family home per parcel is allowed outright, along with crops and livestock. New parcels need at least 5 acres.
jefferson-county:RR-5.notes: Jefferson County's codified RR zone text (JCC 17.304) permits an accessory dwelling unit only in the urban growth area, while the county separately publishes a countywide rural ADU policy at jeffersoncountyor.gov. The two sources disagree, so this ships as a question for the county. Check with Jefferson County Community Development.

jefferson-county:RR-10.name: Rural Residential (RR-10)
jefferson-county:RR-10.plainEnglish: Low density rural homesites in an open space setting. One single family home per parcel is allowed outright, along with crops and livestock. New parcels need at least 10 acres.
jefferson-county:RR-10.notes: Jefferson County's codified RR zone text (JCC 17.304) permits an accessory dwelling unit only in the urban growth area, while the county separately publishes a countywide rural ADU policy at jeffersoncountyor.gov. The two sources disagree, so this ships as a question for the county. Check with Jefferson County Community Development.

jefferson-county:RR-20.name: Rural Residential (RR-20)
jefferson-county:RR-20.plainEnglish: Low density rural homesites in an open space setting. One single family home per parcel is allowed outright, along with crops and livestock. New parcels need at least 20 acres.
jefferson-county:RR-20.notes: Jefferson County's codified RR zone text (JCC 17.304) permits an accessory dwelling unit only in the urban growth area, while the county separately publishes a countywide rural ADU policy at jeffersoncountyor.gov. The two sources disagree, so this ships as a question for the county. Check with Jefferson County Community Development.

jefferson-county:ERD.name: Existing Rural Development (ERD)
jefferson-county:ERD.plainEnglish: Recognizes rural development that already existed, residential and commercial, and lets those uses continue without a nonconforming use designation. Uses legally established before March 11, 1981 continue outright.

jefferson-county:CRRR.name: Crooked River Ranch Residential Zone (CRRR)
jefferson-county:CRRR.plainEnglish: Residential zone for Crooked River Ranch. One single family home or manufactured home per parcel is allowed outright, along with crops, livestock and public parks.

jefferson-county:TRRA.name: Three Rivers Recreation Area Zone (TRRA)
jefferson-county:TRRA.plainEnglish: Recreation area zone near Lake Billy Chinook. One single family home or manufactured home per parcel is allowed outright, plus seasonal RV or tent camping with an approved septic setup.

jefferson-county:MUE.name: Mixed Use Employment (MUE)
jefferson-county:MUE.plainEnglish: Employment zone for business parks, offices, light manufacturing, warehousing and retail. Housing is not permitted as a standalone use.

crook-county:EFU-1.name: Exclusive Farm Use Zone EFU-1 (Post-Paulina Area)
crook-county:EFU-1.plainEnglish: Farmland preservation zone in the post-paulina area. Farm use is the primary use and dwellings follow state farm-use tests. Check with Crook County planning before assuming a home site.

crook-county:EFU-2.name: Exclusive Farm Use Zone EFU-2 (Prineville Valley-Lone Pine Areas)
crook-county:EFU-2.plainEnglish: Farmland preservation zone in the prineville valley-lone pine areas. Farm use is the primary use and dwellings follow state farm-use tests. Check with Crook County planning before assuming a home site.

crook-county:EFU-3.name: Exclusive Farm Use Zone EFU-3 (Powell Butte Area)
crook-county:EFU-3.plainEnglish: Farmland preservation zone in the powell butte area. Farm use is the primary use and dwellings follow state farm-use tests. Check with Crook County planning before assuming a home site.

crook-county:RRM-5.name: Recreation Residential Mobile Zone, RR(M)-5
crook-county:RRM-5.plainEnglish: Rural residential zone where a single family home or manufactured home is allowed outright on each lot, along with limited farming. New parcels need at least 5 acres.

crook-county:R-5.name: Rural Residential Zone, R-5
crook-county:R-5.plainEnglish: Low density rural homesites on land committed to nonresource use. Single family homes, including manufactured homes, are allowed outright. New parcels need at least 5 acres.

crook-county:P-R.name: Park Reserve Zone, P-R
crook-county:P-R.plainEnglish: Reserve zone for farm use, public reserve areas and wildlife areas. Single family homes are allowed outright only within the Juniper Hills and Jasper Knolls areas named in the chapter.

klamath-county:R-1.name: Rural Residential (R-1)
klamath-county:R-1.plainEnglish: County zone for rural residential living, large lot homesites and small scale hobby farming, buffering urban uses from resource land. New lots need at least 1 acre.

klamath-county:R-2.name: Rural Residential (R-2)
klamath-county:R-2.plainEnglish: County zone for rural residential living, large lot homesites and small scale hobby farming, buffering urban uses from resource land. New lots need at least 2 acres.

klamath-county:R-5.name: Rural Residential (R-5)
klamath-county:R-5.plainEnglish: County zone for rural residential living, large lot homesites and small scale hobby farming, buffering urban uses from resource land. New lots need at least 5 acres.

klamath-county:R-10.name: Rural Residential (R-10)
klamath-county:R-10.plainEnglish: County zone for rural residential living, large lot homesites and small scale hobby farming, buffering urban uses from resource land. New lots need at least 10 acres.

klamath-county:RCR.name: Rural Community Residential (RCR)
klamath-county:RCR.plainEnglish: County zone for residential lots inside rural communities, one dwelling per lot. Minimum lot size is 5,000 sq ft.

klamath-county:RS.name: Suburban Residential (RS)
klamath-county:RS.plainEnglish: County zone for suburban residential lots, one dwelling per lot. Minimum lot size is 10,000 sq ft.

klamath-county:RL.name: Low Density Residential (RL)
klamath-county:RL.plainEnglish: County zone for low density residential lots, one dwelling per lot. Minimum lot size is 7,000 sq ft.

klamath-county:RM.name: Medium Density Residential (RM)
klamath-county:RM.plainEnglish: County zone for medium density housing. One single family home per lot, or one duplex or multifamily dwelling per 8,000 sq ft. Minimum lot size is 5,000 sq ft.

klamath-county:RH.name: High Density Residential (RH)
klamath-county:RH.plainEnglish: County zone for higher density housing at 10 to 24 units per acre. Minimum lot size is 10,000 sq ft.

klamath-county:EFU.name: Exclusive Farm Use (EFU)
klamath-county:EFU.plainEnglish: Farmland preservation zone. Farm use is the primary use and dwellings follow state farm-use tests. New parcel minimums run 80 to 160 acres depending on the C, CG or G subzone. Check with Klamath County planning before assuming a home site.

klamath-county:EFU-C.name: Exclusive Farm Use (EFU-C)
klamath-county:EFU-C.plainEnglish: Farmland preservation subzone. Farm use is the primary use and dwellings follow state farm-use tests. Parcels in this subzone are at least 80 acres.

klamath-county:EFU-CG.name: Exclusive Farm Use (EFU-CG)
klamath-county:EFU-CG.plainEnglish: Farmland preservation subzone. Farm use is the primary use and dwellings follow state farm-use tests. Parcels in this subzone are at least 80 acres.

klamath-county:EFU-G.name: Exclusive Farm Use (EFU-G)
klamath-county:EFU-G.plainEnglish: Farmland preservation subzone. Farm use is the primary use and dwellings follow state farm-use tests. Parcels in this subzone are at least 160 acres.

klamath-county:FR.name: Forestry/Range (FR)
klamath-county:FR.plainEnglish: Mixed farm and forest zone for juniper and sagebrush country in southern Klamath County, more productive than nonresource land but less than farm or forest zones.

klamath-county:NR.name: Non-Resource (NR)
klamath-county:NR.plainEnglish: County zone for land with low farm and forest value that is not important habitat or watershed. It carries fewer resource restrictions than farm or forest zones.

jackson-county:RR-5.name: Rural Residential (RR-5)
jackson-county:RR-5.plainEnglish: Large lot rural residential zone consistent with the rural character and physical capability of the land. Dimensional standards live in LDO Chapter 8, which was not loaded for this build. Check with Jackson County Development Services for lot minimums.

jackson-county:RR-2.5.name: Rural Residential (RR-2.5)
jackson-county:RR-2.5.plainEnglish: Large lot rural residential zone consistent with the rural character and physical capability of the land. Dimensional standards live in LDO Chapter 8, which was not loaded for this build. Check with Jackson County Development Services for lot minimums.

jackson-county:RR-10.name: Rural Residential (RR-10)
jackson-county:RR-10.plainEnglish: Large lot rural residential zone consistent with the rural character and physical capability of the land. Dimensional standards live in LDO Chapter 8, which was not loaded for this build. Check with Jackson County Development Services for lot minimums.

jackson-county:RR-00.name: Rural Residential (RR-00)
jackson-county:RR-00.plainEnglish: Large lot rural residential zone consistent with the rural character and physical capability of the land. Dimensional standards live in LDO Chapter 8, which was not loaded for this build. Check with Jackson County Development Services for lot minimums.

jackson-county:EFU.name: Exclusive Farm Use (EFU)
jackson-county:EFU.plainEnglish: Farmland conservation zone implementing Statewide Planning Goal 3. Farm use is the primary use and dwellings follow state farm-use tests. Check with Jackson County Development Services before assuming a home site.

jackson-county:WR.name: Woodland Resource (WR)
jackson-county:WR.plainEnglish: Forest conservation zone implementing Statewide Planning Goal 4. Residential use is heavily restricted. Check with Jackson County Development Services before assuming a home site.

jackson-county:FR.name: Forest Resource (FR)
jackson-county:FR.plainEnglish: Forest conservation zone implementing Statewide Planning Goal 4. Residential use is heavily restricted. Check with Jackson County Development Services before assuming a home site.

jackson-county:OSR.name: Open Space Reserve (OSR)
jackson-county:OSR.plainEnglish: Open space conservation zone grouped with the county's forest districts under Statewide Planning Goal 4. Check with Jackson County Development Services before assuming a home site.

jackson-county:UR-1.name: Urban Residential (UR-1)
jackson-county:UR-1.plainEnglish: County urban residential district for single and multiple family homes in urbanized areas with public services, at planned densities up to 10 dwellings per acre.

jackson-county:UR-4.name: Urban Residential (UR-4)

medford:SFR-4.name: Single-Family Residential (SFR-4)
medford:SFR-4.plainEnglish: Historic low density, large lot single family neighborhoods that also allow all middle housing types. Density runs 2.5 to 4.0 dwelling units per gross acre.
medford:SFR-4.notes: ORS 197A.425 requires cities over 2,500 people to allow at least one accessory dwelling unit on lots zoned for detached single family homes inside the urban growth boundary. Local siting and design standards apply. Check with the City of Medford for its standards.

medford:SFR-6.name: Single-Family Residential (SFR-6)
medford:SFR-6.plainEnglish: Standard density single family neighborhoods that also allow duplexes, triplexes, quadplexes, townhouses and cottage clusters. Density runs 4.0 to 6.0 dwelling units per gross acre.
medford:SFR-6.notes: ORS 197A.425 requires cities over 2,500 people to allow at least one accessory dwelling unit on lots zoned for detached single family homes inside the urban growth boundary. Local siting and design standards apply. Check with the City of Medford for its standards.

medford:SFR-10.name: Single-Family Residential (SFR-10)
medford:SFR-10.plainEnglish: Higher density single family neighborhoods that also allow duplexes, triplexes, quadplexes, townhouses and cottage clusters. Density runs 6.0 to 10.0 dwelling units per gross acre.
medford:SFR-10.notes: ORS 197A.425 requires cities over 2,500 people to allow at least one accessory dwelling unit on lots zoned for detached single family homes inside the urban growth boundary. Local siting and design standards apply. Check with the City of Medford for its standards.
